message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick | A masterclass in psychological dread with iconic imagery. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Ari Aster | A chilling family saga that blends supernatural terror with raw emotion. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Jordan Peele | Smart satire meets genuine scares; a fresh take on social horror. |
| 4 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Ari Aster | Daylight horror that turns a pastoral festival into a nightmare. |
| 5 | **It Follows** | 2014 | David Robert Mitchell | An inventive premise where the threat is relentless and inevitable. |
| 6 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | John Krasinski | Tension built around silence—perfect for a nerve‑wracking experience. |
| 7 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Jennifer Kent | Psychological horror that explores grief and motherhood. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | James Wan | A well‑crafted paranormal thriller that sparked a franchise. |
| 9 | **Suspiria (1977)** | 1977 | Dario Argento | Visually stunning, with a haunting score that lingers long after the credits. |
|10 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Robert Eggers | Slow‑burn dread set in Puritan New England, with meticulous period detail. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want a slow‑building psychological scare or an outright jump‑scare binge!
